title: Semantic library above Foreign Runtime binding authority
summary: The durable architecture separates meaning from binding: unixsocket.cls is the application-facing Unix IPC semantic layer, while Foreign Runtime is the native-call, resource-lifetime and ABI authority that reaches libc.
invariants: Applications should see UnixSocket, UnixAddress, UnixMessage, UnixDescriptor and semantic poll objects rather than raw msghdr/cmsghdr machinery.
Foreign Runtime is the binding mechanism; it does not own Unix-domain application semantics.
Do not reintroduce a Unix-socket-specific native shared library unless a demonstrated Foreign Runtime limitation makes the semantic contract impossible to express safely.
The v0.3 native implementation is retained conceptually as a semantic oracle/history, not as the preferred system boundary.
procedure: Place new Unix IPC semantics in unixsocket.cls; place generally reusable FFI/lifetime/ABI capabilities in Foreign Runtime.

provenance.claim: Architecture defines Foreign Runtime as native binding authority, unixsocket.cls as semantic library, and the managed sendmsg/recvmsg graph.
Foreign Runtime v0.22.3 introduced managed pointer-field graphs, transitive pinning, cycle rejection, and exact binary buffer slices.
provenance.note: Capability that made safe msghdr binding possible.
